# Engine Run-On (Dieseling) Suddenly Getting Much Worse

If you are troubleshooting a 1995 Chevy S-10 Blazer with the 4.3L Vortec V6, specifically a VIN W model equipped with a PCM and OBD-I electronics, you might be facing a situation where an intermittent "dieseling" condition has suddenly become chronic. At 230,000 miles on original components, the engine presents a classic transitional-year scenario: it uses an OBD-II style connector but operates on older logic.

The symptom is distinct: the engine sputters for a second or two after shutting off the ignition. Initially, this only occurred after extended driving or when the coolant was hot. Recently, however, the run-on has become consistent almost every time you turn the key off. You have likely already performed a deep dive into the usual suspects. You've adjusted timing from 10 degrees retarded to 0 TDC, replaced the distributor assembly (including the ICM and pickup coil), swapped out the ignition coil for an MSD unit, and verified the timing chain has only 3.5 degrees of play, which is within GM specs.
